question: What tire inflation pressure is specified for the main wheels during the daily check?
explanation: AFM 4A.5 gives 4.7 bar (68 PSI) for the main wheels and 6.0 bar (87 PSI) for the nose wheel.

question: What tire inflation pressure is specified for the nose wheel during the daily check?
explanation: AFM 4A.5: the nose wheel is checked to 6.0 bar (87 PSI), higher than the 4.7 bar (68 PSI) specified for the main wheels.

question: During the pre-flight walk-around, what is the minimum typical visible length of bare piston required on the MAIN landing gear struts?
explanation: AFM 4A.6.1 specifies a minimum typical visible bare-piston length of 4 cm (1.6 in) on each main gear strut, versus 15 cm (5.9 in) on the nose gear strut.

question: During the pre-flight walk-around, what is the minimum typical visible length of bare piston required on the NOSE landing gear strut?
explanation: AFM 4A.6.1 specifies at least 15 cm (5.9 in) of visible bare piston on the nose gear strut, versus only 4 cm (1.6 in) on each main gear strut.

question: During the cabin pre-flight check, the variable elevator backstop function is tested. What must the control stick do as the power lever is moved from IDLE to MAX?

options.text: Move fully aft to the backstop

explanation: AFM 4A.6.1: with the stick held fully aft, advancing the power lever to MAX should cause the stick to move slightly forward as the variable elevator stop engages.

question: What idle RPM should be observed after starting each engine?
explanation: AFM 4A.6.3 specifies checking idle RPM at 710 ± 30 RPM after each engine start.

question: What is the maximum continuous starter motor operating time during engine start?
explanation: AFM 4A.6.3 cautions not to operate the starter motor for more than 10 seconds, to avoid overheating it.

question: Below what ambient temperature might the engine not start on the first attempt, requiring a 60-second wait between attempts?
explanation: AFM 4A.6.3 notes that at ambient temperatures below -22 °C the engine may not start on the first attempt, requiring a 60-second wait between attempts.

question: If oil pressure has not moved out of the red range within how many seconds of starting, should the ENGINE MASTER be switched OFF and the problem investigated?
explanation: AFM 4A.6.3 warns that if oil pressure has not left the red range within 3 seconds of starting, ENGINE MASTER should be set OFF and the problem investigated.

question: During taxi, what fuel selector test may be performed on both engines simultaneously?

options.text: Cycling both FUEL PUMP switches ON and OFF ten times
Running both engines for approximately 30 seconds with CROSSFEED selected
Running both engines for 5 minutes with both selectors OFF
Alternating ALTERNATOR switches OFF for 60 seconds

explanation: AFM 4A.6.5 describes testing the crossfeed function by running both engines about 30 seconds with CROSSFEED selected; operating in crossfeed for any longer, other than this test, is prohibited.

question: During the before take-off ECU/fuel pump test sequence, what propeller speed range is checked below 1000 RPM at idle?

options.text: Propeller RPM checked at exactly 710 rpm
Propeller RPM checked below 1000 rpm at IDLE before the test starts
Propeller RPM checked above 1800 rpm at IDLE

explanation: AFM 4A.6.6 requires confirming propeller RPM is below 1000 rpm at IDLE with the parking brake set before starting the ECU TEST sequence.

question: During the ECU test sequence, propeller RPM should increase above what value before decreasing, demonstrating each ECU channel?
explanation: AFM 4A.6.6 shows the ECU test sequence cycling propeller RPM above 1800 rpm and back down, twice per channel, for both ECU A and ECU B.

question: During the available-power check before take-off, at what RPM should the engine stabilize with the power lever at MAX for 10 seconds?
explanation: AFM 4A.6.6 expects RPM to stabilize between 2250 and 2300 RPM, with LOAD stabilizing between 89% and 100%, during the available-power check.

question: During the available-power check before take-off, between what LOAD percentages should the engine stabilize at MAX power?
explanation: AFM 4A.6.6: LOAD should stabilize between 89% and 100% (varying with density altitude and OAT) during the available-power check.

question: Is take-off with a fuel selector in the CROSSFEED position permitted?

options.text: Yes, but only for the critical (left) engine
Yes, if the imbalance is below 1 US gal
Yes, provided both engines are running normally

explanation: AFM 4A.6.6 carries a direct warning: take-off with CROSSFEED selected is prohibited.

question: For a standard (flaps UP) take-off, what is the minimum airspeed for nose wheel lift-off (vR)?
explanation: AFM 4A.6.7(a): the standard take-off procedure uses vR = min. 76 KIAS for nose wheel lift-off, regardless of weight band.

question: For a short-field take-off (flaps APP) up to 1900 kg, what is the minimum vR for nose wheel lift-off?
explanation: AFM 4A.6.7(b): the short-field procedure with flaps APP uses vR = min. 71 KIAS up to 1900 kg, rising to 74 KIAS above 1900 kg.

question: For a short-field take-off (flaps APP) above 1900 kg, what is the minimum vR?
explanation: AFM 4A.6.7(b): above 1900 kg the short-field vR rises to 74 KIAS, versus 71 KIAS up to 1900 kg.

question: Before selecting the landing gear UP after take-off, what should be done to the brakes?

options.text: Apply the parking brake instead of toe brakes
Pump the brakes three times to test them
Apply the brakes firmly, to stop wheel rotation before gear retraction
Release the brakes fully to avoid dragging

explanation: AFM 4A.6.7 notes that firmly applying the brakes before selecting gear UP avoids damage and excessive wear of the main wheels.

question: What is the standard climb power setting used in the initial climb check?
explanation: AFM 4A.6.8 sets climb power at 92%, even though the engine manufacturer recommends a cruise power setting of 75%.

question: If oil or coolant temperature reaches the yellow range during climb, what adjustment is recommended?

options.text: Increase airspeed by 10 kts and reduce power by 10%
Reduce airspeed by 10 kts and increase power by 10%
Shut down and feather the affected engine immediately
Switch to ECU B on the affected engine

explanation: AFM 4A.6.8 recommends increasing airspeed 10 kts and reducing power 10% for better engine cooling if oil/coolant temperature reaches the yellow range in climb.

question: What recommended cruise power setting does the engine manufacturer suggest, even though the checklist itself sets cruise power up to 92%?
explanation: AFM 4A.6.9 notes the engine manufacturer's own recommendation of a 75% cruise power setting, distinct from the checklist's own "up to 92%" figure.

question: When transferring fuel from the auxiliary tanks, at what main-tank fuel quantity should both AUX PUMP switches be set to ON?

options.text: 5 US gal or less in each main tank
17 US gal or less in each main tank
25 US gal or less in each main tank

explanation: AFM 4A.6.9: fuel transfer begins once each main tank reaches 17 US gal or less, and continues until the main tanks are full again.

question: Roughly what rate does fuel transfer from the auxiliary tanks into the main tanks?
explanation: AFM 4A.6.9 states the fuel quantity indicator should show a transfer rate of approximately 1 US gal per minute.

question: Why must both AUX PUMP switches always be operated simultaneously?

options.text: To prevent additional lateral (left/right) fuel imbalance
To avoid overheating the fuel selector valves
Because a single pump cannot generate sufficient pressure alone
To synchronize with the ECU VOTER switches

explanation: AFM 4A.6.9/7.9.5 both note that operating the AUX PUMP switches together avoids adding further lateral fuel imbalance.

question: The GFC 700's Vertical Speed (VS) mode is limited to what maximum climb and descent rates?
explanation: AFM 4A.6.8/4A.6.9/4A.6.10 state the VS mode is limited to 1500 ft/min climb and 3000 ft/min descent.

question: The GFC 700's Flight Level Change (FLC) mode is limited to what airspeed range?
explanation: AFM 4A.6.8/4A.6.9/4A.6.10 state FLC mode is limited to airspeeds between 90 and 180 KIAS.

question: Before landing, up to 1900 kg, what is the minimum airspeed with flaps UP during the approach?
explanation: AFM 4A.6.11: up to 1900 kg the approach minimum with flaps UP is 86 KIAS, versus 92 KIAS above 1900 kg.

question: What is the final approach speed with flaps LDG, above 1900 kg?
explanation: AFM 4A.6.11: above 1900 kg, the final approach speed with flaps LDG is a minimum of 86 KIAS, versus 84 KIAS up to 1900 kg.

question: During a go-around, what flap position is initially selected?

options.text: No change from the current position

explanation: AFM 4A.6.12: the go-around checklist selects flaps to APP first, retracting fully to UP only once a positive rate of climb is established.

question: During a go-around, what minimum airspeed is targeted?
explanation: AFM 4A.6.12 targets a minimum of 90 KIAS during the go-around, with POWER lever at MAX and flaps initially at APP.

question: Before engine shutdown, for how long, and at what power setting, must the engine run to avoid heat damage to the turbo charger?
explanation: AFM 4A.6.14 requires running the engine at least 1 minute at 10% load before shutdown, to avoid turbocharger heat damage.

question: After switching ENGINE MASTER OFF during shutdown, what should be confirmed before switching ELECT. MASTER OFF?

options.text: That the G1000 engine indications are red X'd or yellow X'd
That the fuel selectors are both in CROSSFEED
That the propeller has completely stopped rotating
That cabin heat has been selected OFF

explanation: AFM 4A.6.14 cautions to wait until engine indications are X'd before switching ELECT. MASTER OFF, so engine and flight data can be saved to non-volatile memory.
